input: nums is a dense ordinary Array of safe-integer Numbers. The requested target is exactly zero and is not an input parameter. Let n be its length and B its maximum absolute value, or zero for empty input. The shared domain requires 0 <= n <= 4294967295 and mathematical 2 * B <= 9007199254740991. The number Q of distinct qualifying triples must be <= 4294967295; the input, sorted copy and output must fit both runtimes. Lengths n < 3, including empty input, explicitly return an empty result; this authored extension is not a claim that the frozen problem admits those lengths. Inputs must fit both runtimes. NaN, infinities, negative zero, non-integers, BigInt, sparse arrays, accessors, proxies and concurrent mutation are excluded. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: A fresh Array of distinct, fresh 3-element Arrays of safe-integer Number values. Each tuple is nondecreasing, uses distinct input indices with multiplicities available in nums, and has mathematical sum zero. Every qualifying value tuple appears exactly once. The outer result is in deterministic lexicographic numeric order; its order is part of this paired declaration even if the problem accepts order-insensitively. No solution or n < 3 yields an empty Array.
mutation_aliasing: nums, its order, length and elements remain unchanged. Sorting operates only on a new copy. The outer result and every tuple are separately allocated and do not alias nums, the sorted copy, the mutable prefix or each other. The helper's copy, prefix, recursion and result are local; the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: S = 9007199254740991; 0 <= n <= 4294967295; B is the maximum input absolute value or zero. Mathematical 2 * B <= 9007199254740991. Every pair sum and JavaScript sort-comparator subtraction lies in [-2 * B, 2 * B], within [-S, S]. There is at most one residual subtraction from zero, so every residual has absolute value at most B. Comparisons compare these exact bounded values directly and do not subtract pair sums from residuals. Count/index expressions, including count - remaining + 1 in Python, count - remaining in JavaScript, count - 1, index + 1 and pointer updates, stay in [-4, 4294967295], and arity/remaining stay in [2, 4]. No products or accumulated full tuple sums are evaluated. All arithmetic intermediates are exact safe-integer Number values; no bitwise coercion is used. The bounds are mathematical preconditions, not floating-point validation checks.
complexity: For n inputs and Q returned triples, T_sort(n) + O(n^2 + Q + 1) time and O(n + Q + S_sort(n) + 1) total auxiliary storage including the result, where T_sort and S_sort are this engine's numeric Array.sort time and workspace. ECMAScript does not guarantee sort complexity. With O(n log(n + 1)) sort time and O(n + 1) sort workspace, this becomes O(n log(n + 1) + n^2 + Q + 1) time and O(n + Q + 1) space, or O(n + 1) space excluding the result. Other operations assume constant-cost Number/indexing and amortized Array append/pop. Recursion has at most 2 simultaneous search calls, prefix length at most 1, and O(3) copying per emitted tuple.

helpers.name: sortedKSum
helpers.contract: Only arity 3 and 4 are admitted. Sorts a new copy, then emits each distinct nondecreasing arity-tuple that sums to target, in lexicographic order, using distinct input indices. The helper requires n <= 4294967295, at most 4294967295 output tuples, 2 * B <= 9007199254740991, and abs(target) + (arity - 2) * B <= 9007199254740991, where B is the largest input absolute value or zero. Nested search keeps prefix as the selected sorted values, start beyond their indices, remaining as the number still needed, and residual as target minus the prefix sum; the prefix sum is a mathematical invariant, not an extra arithmetic calculation. Ascending distinct index choices suppress repeated prefixes. The two-pointer base case discards a low endpoint when its pair sum is too small, or a high endpoint when too large; after a match it advances both and skips equal endpoint values. Hence distinct pairs are emitted in increasing first-value order. No pruning or helper contract for other arities is claimed.
helpers.cost: One outer helper call; the complete 1301-byte UTF-8 definition, through the newline after its closing brace, is byte-identical in 0015.js and 0018.js. This includes the nested search definition, all call sites, comments, sorting comparator callback, copy and output construction. It is charged in full in each standalone candidate. Search takes O(n^2 + Q + 1) time for this entry point; copying and sorting costs are included in the stated overall complexity. Separator blank lines are charged in total source bytes.

source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 1379 UTF-8 bytes, including the 1301-byte shared helper, its nested search and inline comparator callback, comments, separator newlines, Solution wrapper, call site and terminal newline. Shared spelling is not a free library: all helper bytes are charged separately in each candidate. Standard sorting time/workspace is charged in complexity. No imports, generated source or hidden expansion exists. Any eventual judge adapter is additional charged source.
evidence_boundary: Independently authored dev_fit candidate outside frozen source sets. No candidate execution, predecessor equivalence, behavioral qualification, benchmark acceptance or M1 progress is claimed. The mandatory isolated judge is unavailable; static checks do not establish runtime correctness. Independent source-bound qualification must cover short inputs, repeated values, repeated zeros, positive/negative and mixed signs, multiple/no solutions, distinct-index multiplicities, deterministic order, fresh result rows, input preservation, residual and comparator numeric boundaries, and sort/runtime complexity assumptions before promotion.
